stage1.impression: A calm, believable late-afternoon living room: squared camera, sun through tall glazing, the pair placed symmetrically around a walnut credenza, with the green cabinets lit from inside. It is close to editorial, but the sunlit plaster at the left is a flat, textureless field near white. The left cabinet sits duller than the right. Only the right speaker throws its coloured light, and that goes onto the wall, not into the frame's floor. The insides of the cabinets glow in a saturated lime that reads slightly CG.

blocking_9: Sunlit plaster keeps visible texture: no wall region larger than 100 px with lum_range under 12, and nothing on the wall above lum 235
Both cabinets lit equally by the sun: their interior medians within 15 levels of each other
Each speaker casts a visible green pool of transmitted light onto the floor inside the frame
The cover cloth reads its own colour: delta-E 2000 to #6F7F66 at or below 6
A calm wall zone for the heading 'A pair of Poison.' with no sun-patch edge crossing it

defects.what: Sunlit plaster flat and near white (median 241, range 6-8): no plaster texture, reads as a CG card
Sun patch at median 238 with 0.26% clipped; its hard edges cross where the heading would sit
Left cabinet's interior dimmer than the right's (median 77 vs 109); the pair does not read as equally lit
Right speaker's transmitted green falls behind it onto the wall and baseboard; no green pool on the floor in front of either speaker
Cover cloth measures RGB 86,136,94, delta-E 9.1 to #6F7F66: green spill from inside the cabinet makes it too saturated
Lit interior ribs and batts read lime (72,126,63), delta-E 27 to the #B2C9A2 reference: saturated, slightly emissive look
The clear Cumulus record player hardly separates from the lit wall behind it; it reads as a smudge
A long hard diagonal sill-shadow edge runs across the whole floor in front of the product and pulls the eye out of frame left
Window strip with a thick pale frame and busy orange forest at the left edge competes with the left speaker

changes.problem: The sun enters at an angle that lights the right cabinet more than the left and throws the transmitted green onto the back wall instead of onto the floor in frame, so the main idea (sun through both cabinets) only half reads.

evidence.measured: left interior median 77 vs right [1030,410,1190,450] median 109; floor in front of right speaker [1010,690,1210,740] RGB 86,68,38, no green

change.to: azimuth -105, elevation 13 (from the left and slightly behind the speakers, so the transmitted light falls forward and right onto the floor)

changes.expected: Both cabinets lit through, interiors within 15 levels of each other; a soft green pool on the floor beside and in front of each speaker

changes.problem: The sunlit plaster burns to a flat cream field with no texture, which is the biggest CG tell in the frame.
changes.expected: Sunlit plaster around 220-230 with visible trowel texture, nothing over 235

changes.problem: The cover cloth is lit mostly by green light from inside the cabinet, so its colour is off and the hero colour is untrue.
changes.expected: Neutral front light dominates the cover; the cloth reads grey-green near #6F7F66

changes.problem: The lit interiors read as a saturated lime glow rather than light through tinted acrylic onto pale batts.

change.to: 5200 K plus a finish-stage green-hue saturation of -15% limited to the cabinet interiors' luminance band (100-200)

changes.expected: Interiors read paler and closer to the reference tint, with the batts' texture visible

changes.problem: The heading sits over the wall, but the wall's top band is broken by sun-patch edges, so a heading there would fight the light.

evidence.measured: profile drops from 240 to 129 at the patch edge at about x 850; the edge step is 12 px wide

change.setting: window 0 / window 1 sizes (the patches on the wall)
change.to: lower the top of the window 1 opening to 2.2 m (size [1.45, 2.2]) so the sun patch on the wall ends below y about 120 px, leaving the top band in even shade for type

changes.expected: A calm, evenly shaded band at the top of the wall above both horns, range under 30 levels

changes.problem: The clear record player is lost against the lit wall and reads as a smudge.

evidence.measured: median 113, near the neutral wall behind it; no dark edge to hold it

change.setting: prop record player position (allowed to move)
change.from: left of centre, in front of the bright patch
change.to: move it 0.25 m right so it sits in front of the shadowed wall between the patches, and turn it 15 deg to show the platter's rim

changes.expected: The acrylic's edges read bright against a darker wall; it reads as an object at a glance

changes.problem: A long hard sill-shadow edge cuts diagonally across the whole foreground floor and leads the eye out of the frame.

evidence.measured: visible hard step along about 1000 px of floor in the crop

change.to: open 0.35 on prop 12 so the sheer softens the lower window's light on the floor

changes.expected: The floor light becomes a softer, diffused gradient; the speakers' green pools become the floor's brightest accents

changes.problem: The pale window frame and the bright orange forest at the far left compete with the left speaker for attention.

evidence.measured: median 112, p95 164, warm orange high saturation at the frame edge

changes.expected: The left edge settles into a darker frame that bounds the picture instead of pulling at it

out_of_scope.request: The horn's throat (compression driver) reads as a black hole in the centre of each horn
out_of_scope.why: It is part of the speaker; lighting cannot open it without changing the part

out_of_scope.request: Check the cabinet acrylic's transmission colour and the batts' albedo against #B2C9A2; the interior's lime may be partly the material, not the light
out_of_scope.why: It is the speaker's colour and material, which are fixed
